review_candidates.description: POSITION SUMMARY The Chief Real Estate Officer (CREO) directs the Authority’s real estate strategy, development, redevelopment, modernization, maintenance, and long-term preservation of its housing portfolio. Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer/Executive Director, the CREO leads Real Estate Development, Facilities & Modernization, and Maintenance Operations across the full asset lifecycle. The CREO improves portfolio performance, addresses distressed properties and deferred maintenance, and leverages public and private investment to support long-term sustainability. The role oversees complex affordable housing transactions and repositioning strategies, including RAD, LIHTC, mixed-finance development, acquisition, rehabilitation, new construction, recapitalization, and disposition. The CREO ensures compliance with applicable housing, construction, procurement, environmental, accessibility, fair housing, and building regulations. ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES Executive Leadership and Portfolio Strategy • Provides executive leadership for the Authority’s physical real estate portfolio and establishes comprehensive strategies for development, redevelopment, preservation, modernization, maintenance, and long-term asset sustainability. • Develops and implements a multi-year real estate and capital investment strategy consistent with the Authority’s strategic plan, HUD requirements, financial capacity, local housing needs, and organizational priorities. • Evaluates the physical, financial, operational, and market performance of Authorityowned properties and recommends appropriate strategies, including preservation, rehabilitation, recapitalization, redevelopment, conversion, disposition, acquisition, replacement, or other repositioning alternatives. • Advises the CEO and Board of Commissioners regarding major real estate investments, development opportunities, portfolio conditions, capital requirements, asset risks, and repositioning strategies. Real Estate Development • Directs all Authority-sponsored real estate development and redevelopment activities from initial concept through feasibility, planning, financing, construction, lease-up, stabilization, and transition to operations. • Directs feasibility studies, site analysis, market analysis, financial modeling, due diligence, environmental review, entitlement, design, financing, construction, and project closeout. • Oversees the procurement and performance of developers, architects, engineers, construction managers, general contractors, environmental consultants, attorneys, financial advisors, development consultants, and other professional service providers. • Establishes project controls for schedule, budget, scope, risk, quality, regulatory compliance, and project deliverables. Portfolio Repositioning • Leads the Authority’s portfolio repositioning strategy to improve the long-term physical and financial viability of its housing assets. • Evaluates properties for participation in HUD repositioning programs and other preservation, redevelopment, conversion, or disposition strategies. • Directs transactions involving Rental Assistance Demonstration (RAD), RAD/Section 18 blends, Section 18 demolition and disposition, Streamlined Voluntary Conversion, where applicable, Low-Income Housing Tax Credits, Mixed-finance public housing development, Project-Based Voucher strategies, Acquisition and rehabilitation, New construction, Recapitalization and refinancing, Property disposition, Public-private partnerships, Mixed-income development, Mixed-use development; and, Other HUD-approved repositioning strategies. • Ensures repositioning recommendations are supported by appropriate physical needs assessments, financial analysis, capital planning, market analysis, resident impact analysis, and long-term operating projections. RAD and LIHTC Development • Provides executive oversight of RAD transactions from feasibility through conversion, construction, completion, and stabilization. • Directs LIHTC transactions involving 4% and 9% tax credits, tax-exempt bonds, private debt, soft financing, seller financing, subordinate debt, grants, and other development funding sources. • Reviews development budgets, sources and uses, operating pro formas, developer fees, reserves, financing assumptions, construction budgets, operating assumptions, and long-term financial projections. • Oversee due diligence and coordination necessary to achieve financial closing and successful project completion. Facilities and Modernization • Provide executive oversight of the Authority’s Facilities & Modernization functions. • Develops a comprehensive capital improvement and modernization strategy based upon property conditions, regulatory requirements, available funding, operational priorities, and portfolio repositioning plans. • Oversees capital planning, physical needs assessments, energy initiatives, infrastructure improvements, building systems, major renovations, modernization projects, and other capital investments. • Ensures projects are appropriately scoped, budgeted, procured, scheduled, monitored, documented, inspected, and closed out. Maintenance Operations • Provides executive leadership and oversight of the Authority’s maintenance organization. • Establishes performance standards and accountability systems for preventive maintenance, routine work orders, emergency maintenance, vacancy preparation, unit turnaround, inspections, grounds maintenance, building systems, and overall property conditions. • Develops strategies to improve maintenance productivity, reduce work-order backlogs, decrease unit turnaround time, control overtime and material costs, improve preventive maintenance, and increase resident satisfaction. • Establishes preventive and predictive maintenance programs designed to extend the useful life of Authority assets and reduce emergency repairs. Physical Asset Management and Regulatory Compliance • Establishes standards for the physical performance of the Authority’s housing portfolio. • Ensures properties are maintained in compliance with applicable HUD physical inspection requirements, including NSPIRE, and applicable state and local building, property maintenance, fire, health, environmental, accessibility, and safety codes. • Coordinates corrective action plans resulting from HUD inspections, third-party inspections, insurance inspections, accessibility reviews, environmental findings, or other regulatory assessments. • Ensures appropriate inspection, quality-control, and quality-assurance systems are established for maintenance and capital activities. Distressed Portfolio Recovery and Turnaround • Leads strategies for the stabilization, recovery, repositioning, and long-term preservation of distressed, aging, underperforming, or financially challenged properties. • Assesses portfolio-wide physical and financial conditions and identifies deferred maintenance, capital liabilities, regulatory risks, and operational deficiencies. • Prioritizes capital investments based upon life-safety considerations, regulatory requirements, physical conditions, financial feasibility, available resources, and long-term portfolio strategy. • Develops strategies to leverage RAD, LIHTC, mixed-finance transactions, grants, debt, and other public and private financing sources to address significant capital needs. Capital Planning and Financial Management • Develops short- and long-range capital plans for the Authority’s portfolio. • Coordinates capital investment priorities with the CEO, Finance, Housing Operations, Procurement, and other departments. • Monitors capital expenditures, development costs, maintenance expenses, construction costs, reserves, and funding utilization. • Identifies and pursues financing and funding opportunities, including federal and state programs, grants, tax credits, bonds, private debt, local funding, energy incentives, and other resources. Procurement and Contract Administration • Ensures procurement activities under the CREO’s authority comply with applicable federal, state, local, HUD, and Authority procurement requirements. • Develops or oversees scopes of work, technical specifications, evaluation criteria, independent cost estimates, and procurement documentation. • Participates in the evaluation and selection of developers, contractors, consultants, architects, engineers, construction managers, and professional service providers. • Ensures change orders, amendments, payment requests, project modifications, and contract extensions are appropriately justified, documented, reviewed, and authorized. Organizational Leadership and Staff Management • Directly and indirectly supervises assigned directors, managers, supervisors, project managers, inspectors, technical staff, modernization personnel, maintenance employees, and other assigned staff. • Establishes clear performance expectations and measurable departmental objectives. • Evaluates organizational structure, staffing levels, workflows, productivity, and departmental responsibilities and recommends changes necessary to improve efficiency and accountability. • Promotes coordination among Real Estate Development, Facilities & Modernization, Maintenance, Housing Operations, Finance, Procurement, Legal, Resident Services, and executive leadership. MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS Education • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university in Real Estate Development, Business Administration, Finance, Architecture, Engineering, Construction Management, Urban Planning, Public Administration, Housing, or a closely related field. • A master’s degree in Real Estate Development, Business Administration, Finance, Urban Planning, Public Administration, or a related discipline is preferred. Experience • Minimum ten (10) years of progressively responsible experience in real estate development, affordable or public housing, asset management, construction, capital planning, facilities, maintenance, or related fields. • Demonstrated experience leading complex affordable housing development or redevelopment projects, financing, multidisciplinary teams, consultants, contractors, and professional service providers.

Conhecimento em Power BI e em ferramentas de IA aplicadas à gestão de projetos. Capacidade analítica, comunicação clara, organização e proatividade.

review_candidates.title: Advanced Practice RN Provider-Life Flight
review_candidates.description: Location: METROHEALTH MEDICAL CENTER Biweekly Hours: 80.00 Shift: 8:00 AM TO 5:00 PM Where Critical Care Meets Flight Medicine Do you thrive in high-acuity environments where every clinical decision matters? Are you ready to practice at the highest level of advanced practice nursing while providing critical care in one of the most dynamic clinical environments? The Department of Emergency Medicine at The MetroHealth System , a nationally recognized academic medical center and principal teaching affiliate of Case Western Reserve University School of Medicine , is seeking an experienced Acute Care Nurse Practitioner (AGACNP or ACNP) to join Metro Life Flight , one of Northeast Ohio’s premier critical care transport programs. This is an exceptional opportunity to provide advanced critical care aboard helicopter and ground critical care transport units. As part of a highly skilled multidisciplinary team of physicians, advanced practice providers, flight nurses, paramedics, pilots, and EMS professionals, you will care for critically ill and injured patients requiring rapid transport to specialized tertiary and quaternary care centers throughout the region. Why Metro Life Flight? Deliver advanced critical care during helicopter and ground transport. Practice with a high degree of autonomy while collaborating closely with Emergency Medicine physicians and multidisciplinary specialists. Care for complex trauma and critically ill medical, surgical, cardiac, neurologic, respiratory, and high-risk obstetrical patients. Utilize advanced critical care procedures, monitoring, medications, and technologies. Participate in education, simulation, quality improvement, and research initiatives. Practice in a unique environment that combines critical care medicine, emergency medicine, and flight medicine. What You’ll Do Assess, stabilize, and manage critically ill and injured adult and pediatric patients during transport. Develop and implement evidence-based treatment plans for complex, time-sensitive clinical conditions. Manage mechanical ventilation, invasive monitoring, vasoactive medications, blood products, and advanced cardiac and critical care therapies. Perform and/or assist with advanced critical care procedures within established scope of practice and program competencies. Collaborate with EMS agencies, trauma teams, intensivists, surgeons, specialty services, and referring and receiving hospitals. Provide comprehensive critical care throughout the transport continuum, from referring facility or scene through arrival at the receiving center. Promote safe transport operations, clinical excellence, and optimal patient outcomes. Contribute to ongoing education, simulation, quality improvement, and clinical research. Why You’ll Love Working Here Academic affiliation with Case Western Reserve University School of Medicine. Practice within a nationally recognized academic health system. Comprehensive onboarding, orientation, and ongoing professional development. Continuing education and opportunities to advance clinical expertise. Teaching and mentoring opportunities with residents, fellows, nurses, paramedics, and other learners. Strong physician and multidisciplinary collaboration. Competitive compensation and comprehensive benefits. The opportunity to practice critical care medicine in a unique prehospital and transport environment. Qualifications Master of Science in Nursing (MSN) or higher. Graduate of an accredited Adult-Gerontology Acute Care Nurse Practitioner (AGACNP) or Acute Care Nurse Practitioner (ACNP) program. Current Ohio RN and APRN licensure and national board certification. Current AHA BLS certification. Eligibility for clinical privileges through The MetroHealth System. Critical care, emergency medicine, trauma, or transport experience preferred. Demonstrated ability to function effectively in high-acuity, rapidly changing clinical environments. Strong communication, clinical judgment, and multidisciplinary collaboration skills. Join Our Mission At Metro Life Flight, every mission presents an opportunity to make a difference when time, expertise, and decisive clinical care matter most. If you are an experienced Acute Care Nurse Practitioner who is passionate about critical care, emergency medicine, and caring for patients in a uniquely challenging environment, we invite you to explore a career with Metro Life Flight . To apply, please submit your CV and cover letter to: Eloy Vázquez, Sr. Provider Recruiter The MetroHealth System Email: evazquez@metrohealth.org

review_candidates.title: Account Manager - French Speaker (SaaS B2B)
review_candidates.description: About Emotion Mobility Emotion Mobility is a PSG-backed global SaaS leader in fleet and mobility management, powering rental, leasing, subscription, and chauffeur operations for hundreds of enterprise clients across 600,000+ vehicles worldwide. Our platforms - Rentway and Carpro - are trusted by leading mobility brands such as Volkswagen, Ford, Europcar, and Hertz, helping them optimize operations and scale with confidence. We operate in a high-growth phase with a target of €50M ARR by 2030, strong Net Revenue Retention, and double-digit EBITDA margins. With offices in Lisbon, Pune, Dubai and Amsterdam and a presence in 90+ countries, we combine global scale with local execution. As a product-led company, we move fast, ship continuously, and focus relentlessly on solving real customer problems - replacing legacy tools with modern, high-performance software built for the mobility industry. Your Mission We are on the lookout for a dynamic and results-driven Account Manager to join our growing team. As the primary liaison between our company andour esteemed customers, you will play a pivotal role in nurturing relationships, addressing customer needs, and driving revenue growth. You will be responsible to understand the challenges faced by our Rentway customers and use our product portfolio to understand how we can address their challenges or convey custom developments needs to the product team. You will directly report to our Global Commercial Director. What You'll Do Act as the primary point of contact for the management of Tier II/III customers, coordinating and scheduling regular meetings with the customers to nurture relationships, gather feedback and provide a 360º overview of their relationship with us, ensuring satisfaction; Prepare meeting agendas and materials in notes shared with the clients for follow-up; Gather information regarding the client's business strategy to understand where our product portfolio fits, and collect information for future product development; Manage Customer Requests, liaising between product and customers regarding specific development requests; Maintain accurate records of customer interactions and resolutions using CRM software, and provide timely updates and follow-up to customers regarding the status of their requests or issues; Develop targeted upselling strategies and campaigns, and identify opportunities for upselling or cross-selling additional products or services to existing customers based on their usage patterns, needs, and objectives; Track and report on upgrade metrics and success rates, identifying areas for improvement and optimization; Negotiate terms, pricing and contract renewals as needed to secure upsell opportunities; Proactively engage customers on the benefits and features of our newest SaaS product; Coordinate with relevant teams to facilitate the seamless implementation of upgrades. What We're Looking For 3 years of experience in an Account role with B2B clients (mandatory) ; Previous experience in Tech/Startup or in the Car Rental industry (mandatory) ; Professional proficiency in French (mandatory: at least B2) ; Proficiency in CRM software and Jira/Confluence would be a strong plus; Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to build rapport and trust with customers; Willing to learn a business from the ground up and not be afraid to suggest and pitch new ideas; Strategic thinking and problem-solving abilities, with a focus on driving customer satisfaction and revenue growth; Being resourceful and gifted with great ownership while managing different deals. Why Join Us Competitive salary with a permanent full-time contract; Work–life balance that works for you, with Friday afternoons off to start your weekend early; Your birthday off - celebrate your day, your way; Flexible benefits designed around your wellbeing; Private healthcare for you and your children; Referral bonus program - bring great people, get rewarded; Two paid days per year for volunteering or charity work; Enjoy free coffee, fresh fruit & monthly team lunches; Join a global, fast-moving team full of energy and ambition, where you can grow in a culture that champions learning, development and continuous progress. For more information on our data processing activities and your rights as a data subject, please consult our privacy policy at Privacy policy | Emotion Mobility .
